Name: General function definition
$math{Injective function (one-to-one mapping function)/Injektiv funktion}
$math{Surjective function/Surjektiv funktion}
Basic relationship: f: A->B, $math{\\A y in B \\E x in A -> f(x)=y}

Name: Strictly monotone function/Strängt monotona funktioner
Basic relationship:
Strictly increasing and strictly decreasing functions
f injective <=> f strictly monotone

Name: Inverse function
Basic relationship:
Bijective function, f: A->B, $math{f^(-1): B->A}, f ($math{D_(f^(-1)) = V_f, V_(f^(-1)) = D_f})
$math{f^(-1)(y)=x -> y=f(x)}, $math{f^(-1)(f(x)) = x}, $math{f(f^(-1)(y))=y}
For every y in V_f gives x in D_f -> f^(-1) inverse to f
Geometrical interpretation: mirroring in y=x

Name: Calculate inverse function
Polynomial function
Number of roots
Number of real roots (Descartes Rule of Signs)
Basic relationship:
Number of positive roots = number of sign variations of f(x) or less than that by an even integer
Number of negative roots = number of sign variations of f(-x) or less than that by an even integer

Name: Number of complex roots
Basic relationship: Real coefficients -> Complex roots always occur in conjugate pairs (a \pm b*i), There is never only one complex root

Name: Location of real roots
Basic relationship: If f(a) and f(b) are opposite signs, there are at least one or an odd number of roots between a and b
Presetted values:
$math{f(x) = 8x^3 - 12x^2 - 2*x + 3 = 0}
f(-1) = -15, f(0) = 3
f(1) = -3, f(2) = 15
therefore real root exists in each of intervals:
(-1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 2)

Name: Relationship between coefficients p_i and roots x_i
Basic relationship:
-p_1 = sum of all roots
p_2 = sum of all products of roots taken two at a time
-p_3 = sum of all products of roots taken three at a time
$math{(-1)^n * p_n = product of all roots}
